name: The Hornbeam of Freisaalweg

location.address: Freisaalweg, beside the public Parkplatz Akademiestraße car park, Nonntal, Salzburg

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Salzburg (register entry NDM00202, designated 1986, protected area 0.049 ha)

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freisaal (independent Wikipedia article on the Freisaal district, states the tree's estimated age directly: 'eine mehrstämmige Hainbuche, deren Alter auf mehr als 200 Jahre geschätzt wird')
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Naturdenkmal_Hainbuche_am_Freisaalweg,_Salzburg.JPG (dated, geotagged photo, 22 May 2014, coordinates match the register centroid to within a few metres)
access: Free. Stands beside the public Parkplatz Akademiestraße car park (220 spaces) in Nonntal; publicly viewable, no gate or restriction found.
transport: Bus line 20 (Nonntal route), stop Akademiestraße or Hofhaymer-Allee; about a 15-20 minute walk south from Salzburg's Altstadt (Residenzplatz)
verify_notes: Multi-stemmed hornbeam, register text calls it 'besonders ebenmäßige mächtige' (notably symmetrical and mighty) with a strikingly spherical/globe-shaped crown ('auffallend kugeliger Krone', per the Freisaal Wikipedia article). It is the last surviving tree from the garden of a Gründerzeit (turn-of-the-century) villa on Freisaalweg that later housed Salzburg University's Institute of Biology until 1986, when the institute moved to the NAWI building nearby. Declared a Naturdenkmal on 23 January 1986 (register id NDM00202). Age is a real source's own estimate ('more than 200 years'), kept as vague as given, not sharpened. Protected-area figures differ slightly between two independent transcriptions of the same register (490 sq m per the Wikipedia list's hectare figure vs 453 sq m per the Freisaal article), a minor rounding discrepancy, not chased further. A tertiary source, austria-forum.org's AustriaWiki mirror, lists this same tree under a different register id (NDM00100) than the Wikipedia list and our own register import (NDM00202); likely an error in that mirror, noted but not resolved. Alive confirmation rests on a dated 2014 photograph; no more recent sighting found this pass, hence flagged rather than confident. No girth published anywhere found; a reader with a tape measure would answer the gap in one message.

name: The Courtyard Oak of Aigner Straße

location.address: Aigner Straße 9, in the courtyard behind the apartment blocks, Aigen, Salzburg

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Salzburg (register entry NDM00251, designated 2005, protected area 0.033 ha, quotes the tree's own access text)

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datei:Eiche_an_der_Aigner_Strasse_9_(1).JPG (independent dated, geotagged photo by a different photographer, 30 May 2014, coordinates match the register centroid closely, uploaded for the Wiki Loves Earth 2014 contest)
access: Free and explicitly unrestricted. The register's own text states it plainly: 'Die Eiche an der Aigner Straße 9 steht im Innenhof mehrerer Wohnblocks. Sie ist trotzdem ohne Einschränkungen zugänglich' (stands in the courtyard of several apartment blocks; nevertheless it is accessible without restriction).
transport: Salzburg Aigen station (Obus line 7 and S-Bahn S3), on Aigner Straße itself, a short walk to the courtyard
verify_notes: Trunk splits into several strong limbs at a height of 2.5 to 4 metres, per the register's own description. Designated a Naturdenkmal in 2005, one of the more recently protected trees in the city (NDM00251). Stands in the shared courtyard of an apartment-block group in the Aigen I cadastral area, but the register is explicit that public access is unrestricted, so this is not a case needing the OSM access-tag workaround. No age or girth published in any source found this pass; the register carries no age field for any tree (confirmed project-wide) and no girth was given here. Species: the register calls it simply 'Eiche' (oak) with no species named. This city's other three published oak entries (szb_002, szb_003, szb_006) are all Pedunculate Oak (Quercus robur), the common local urban oak, and this one is treated the same way by that convention; it is not independently confirmed to species level, so the page could invite a reader to confirm from a leaf or acorn photo. Alive confirmation rests on a dated 2014 photograph; no more recent sighting found this pass.

name: The Meadow Oak of Buchholzhofstraße

location.address: Buchholzhofstraße, Kleingmain/Morzg, Salzburg, on the pedestrian and cycle path leading toward Hellbrunner Allee

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Salzburg (register entry NDM00206, designated 1986, protected area 0.0346 ha)

https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:00206_Eiche_an_der_Buchholzhofstra%C3%9Fe.jpg (independent dated, geotagged photo, 16 August 2014, categorised by Commons as Quercus robur, coordinates match the register centroid closely)
access: Free. Stands beside Buchholzhofstraße, whose northern stretch is a public pedestrian and cycle path (Geh- und Radweg) running into the Hellbrunner Allee; no gate or restriction found.
transport: Bus/Obus line 5 or bus line 25 (Morzg route); about a 20-25 minute walk south from Salzburg's Altstadt
verify_notes: Register describes it as a cultural relic (Kulturrelikt), a remnant of the once-extensive, sparsely wooded meadows (Extensivwiesen) that used to stand near the Hellbrunner Allee before the area was built up; the tree itself long predates its 1986 Naturdenkmal designation (NDM00206) by that framing, though no specific age is given by any source. Species confirmed independently: Wikimedia Commons categorises the photographed tree under 'Quercus robur in Austria', which is a second, independent identification beyond the register's bare 'Eiche'. No girth published. Buchholzhofstraße's own history (named 1941 after the Buchholzhof) and its current pedestrian/cycle-path status came from a general search on the street rather than a source naming this specific tree, so the access finding is about the street, not an eyewitness account of the tree; kept as a reasonable inference rather than a certainty. Alive confirmation rests on a dated 2014 photograph; no more recent sighting found this pass.
